chains.title: TFAP2A binds the ref A allele more strongly

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the ref A allele more strongly than the alt G allele at rs642961; the G allele weakens an AP-2-type binding site.
rs642961 lies in an IRF6 craniofacial enhancer; the A>G change reduces enhancer activity.
Reduced enhancer activity lowers IRF6 transcription.
The relevant cells are oral/craniofacial epithelial cells where TFAP2A and IRF6 are expressed.
Lower IRF6 levels in the developing lip epithelium increase cleft lip risk.

predictions: recombinant TFAP2A binds ref-A oligo more than alt-G oligo
rs642961 A>G reduces enhancer activity in oral/craniofacial epithelial cells
risk G allele associates with lower IRF6 expression in relevant epithelial cells
lower IRF6 increases cleft lip risk
falsified_if: EMSA or ChIP shows no ref>alt TFAP2A binding at rs642961
ref-A and alt-G reporters have equal activity in oral epithelial cells
IRF6 expression is not allele-dependently altered in relevant cells

chains.title: null: no TF-mediated allelic effect at rs642961
predictions: no allele-specific TF binding at rs642961
no allele-specific enhancer activity in the relevant cells
association with cleft lip is explained by LD with a linked causal variant or by chance/passenger effect
falsified_if: a reproducible allele-specific TFAP2A binding difference is found for rs642961
a ref-vs-alt reporter shows allele-specific activity in oral/craniofacial epithelial cells

chains.title: TFAP2C, not TFAP2A, mediates the allelic binding effect

links.claim: TFAP2C binds the ref A allele more strongly than the alt G allele at rs642961, with AP-2-family redundancy at this site.
rs642961 lies in an IRF6 craniofacial enhancer whose activity depends on this AP-2-family site.
Allele-specific TFAP2C binding alters IRF6 enhancer output and IRF6 transcription.
The effect occurs in oral/craniofacial epithelial cells expressing TFAP2C and IRF6.
Altered IRF6 dosage in the developing lip increases cleft lip risk.

predictions: recombinant TFAP2C binds ref-A oligo more than alt-G oligo
TFAP2C ChIP at the IRF6 enhancer is allele-specific
TFAP2A knockdown does not abolish the allele-specific enhancer effect
TFAP2C knockdown reduces IRF6 enhancer activity in oral epithelial cells
falsified_if: TFAP2C shows no allele-specific binding at rs642961
TFAP2A, not TFAP2C, is the major allele-specific factor in the relevant cells

chains.title: TFAP2A binds the alt G allele more strongly

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the alt G allele more strongly than the ref A allele at rs642961.
rs642961 lies in an IRF6 craniofacial enhancer and the G allele strengthens its activity.
Increased enhancer activity raises IRF6 transcription.
The effect occurs in oral/craniofacial epithelial cells.
Altered IRF6 dosage in the developing lip changes cleft lip risk.

predictions: recombinant TFAP2A binds alt-G oligo more than ref-A oligo
risk G allele increases enhancer activity in the assay used
the direction of IRF6 expression change is opposite to the ref>alt model
if IRF6 is protective, the alt-G higher-binding model could still fit cleft lip risk
falsified_if: EMSA shows ref A binds TFAP2A more strongly than alt G
reporter assays show the G allele reduces rather than increases enhancer activity

next_experiment: allele-specific EMSA with recombinant TFAP2A and ref-A vs alt-G oligos around rs642961; include TFAP2C as a secondary probe. This is the cheapest direct test of the top chain's binding claim and can separate it from the null no-allelic-effect chain. A ref>alt TFAP2A binding difference supports the TFAP2A chain and weakens the null; absence of allele-specific binding falsifies the primary binding link. EMSA alone cannot prove the IRF6 enhancer, cell-type, or phenotype links.
